title: Directeur marketing
descriptif_court: Pilotez la stratégie marketing, la croissance de la marque et l’expérience client pour transformer les tendances du marché en opportunités concrètes.
descriptif_general:
Le directeur marketing définit les orientations de développement d’une entreprise à partir d’une lecture fine du marché, de ses concurrents et des attentes des consommateurs. Son rôle consiste à identifier les opportunités de croissance les plus prometteuses et à traduire ces analyses en décisions marketing concrètes. Il agit au croisement de la stratégie, de l’innovation, de la communication et de la performance commerciale.

Au quotidien, il suit l’évolution de l’écosystème dans lequel la marque et les produits évoluent. Il s’appuie sur des études de marché, l’analyse des données disponibles et l’observation des tendances pour mieux comprendre l’image de la marque, les usages des clients et les points de friction dans l’expérience client. Cette approche lui permet de nourrir la réflexion sur les futures offres, d’ajuster les messages et de faire évoluer le marketing mix en cohérence avec les besoins du marché.

Le directeur marketing construit la stratégie marketing de l’entreprise en fixant les objectifs, en définissant les plans d’action, en allouant les budgets et en suivant des indicateurs de performance. Il supervise aussi la visibilité de l’entreprise, la génération de trafic, le référencement, les opérations de merchandising ou encore les collaborations avec d’autres marques. Selon le contexte, il peut également jouer un rôle fort sur la communication de marque, la stratégie digitale ou le développement e-commerce.

Ce métier demande une forte capacité de coordination. Le directeur marketing travaille avec les équipes marketing, commerciales, parfois communication, ainsi qu’avec des agences externes. Il veille à la cohérence des actions sur l’ensemble des canaux pour offrir une expérience client homogène. Il participe aussi à la conception des outils d’aide à la vente et à la cartographie des parcours clients afin d’identifier les irritants et d’améliorer la conversion comme la satisfaction.

Le poste implique également une dimension managériale importante. Recrutement, animation des équipes, délégation, accompagnement et développement des collaborateurs font partie intégrante de la fonction. Le directeur marketing doit conjuguer vision stratégique, sens de l’écoute, créativité et rigueur pour faire avancer des projets souvent transverses et engager les équipes autour d’une ambition commune.

Pour quels environnements de travail ?

Le périmètre du poste varie selon la taille et l’activité de l’entreprise. Dans les organisations adressant le grand public, la fonction intègre souvent la marque, la stratégie digitale et parfois l’e-commerce. Dans les entreprises BtoB, elle se concentre davantage sur le marketing mix des produits. Dans les structures de petite taille, le directeur marketing encadre souvent directement une équipe opérationnelle, tandis que dans les grands groupes il pilote plutôt plusieurs responsables marketing et des équipes plus larges.

Pourquoi choisir ce métier ?

Ce métier s’adresse à celles et ceux qui aiment transformer des analyses en décisions, travailler avec plusieurs métiers et donner du sens à des actions marketing variées. Il offre une belle exposition stratégique, une forte dimension relationnelle et une place centrale dans la croissance de l’entreprise. Pour un profil Bac+5, il constitue une évolution naturelle vers des fonctions de pilotage et de direction dans le marketing, la communication ou le digital.
missions_principales: Analyser le marché, les concurrents, les partenaires et les attentes des consommateurs.
Identifier les opportunités de croissance et les orientations de développement.
Définir la stratégie marketing, les objectifs, les plans d’action et les budgets.
Piloter le marketing mix et l’optimisation de l’offre.
Superviser la visibilité de l’entreprise et les actions de génération de trafic.
competences_hard_skills: Maîtrise de la réalisation de plans marketing stratégique.
Excellente maîtrise du marketing digital et des dispositifs digitaux et sociaux.
Connaissance des marchés mondiaux et des environnements internationaux.
Bonne maîtrise des techniques d’analyse de marché et de marketing opérationnel.
Connaissance des médias, de la communication hors médias et de leurs complémentarités.
competences_soft_skills: Aisance relationnelle et sens de l’écoute.
Capacité à animer des équipes transverses.
Capacités managériales et aptitude à déléguer.

title: Directeur de la communication
descriptif_court: Définir et piloter la stratégie de communication pour renforcer l’image, la visibilité et la cohérence de marque d’une organisation.
descriptif_general:
Le directeur de la communication définit et pilote la stratégie de communication d’une entreprise, d’une institution ou d’une organisation. Son rôle est de donner une direction claire aux messages diffusés en interne comme en externe, afin de renforcer l’image, la visibilité et la cohérence de la marque. Il travaille souvent en lien direct avec la direction générale et intervient sur des sujets variés : communication corporate, relations presse, relations publiques, événementiel, communication digitale et communication de crise.

Ce poste s’adresse à des profils de cadre expérimenté capables de prendre de la hauteur sur les enjeux de l’entreprise. Le directeur de la communication recueille les informations stratégiques auprès de la gouvernance, analyse le positionnement de l’organisation et construit un plan de communication annuel. Il veille à ce que chaque action, chaque support et chaque prise de parole soit aligné avec la stratégie globale et avec l’identité de marque. Il joue aussi un rôle de conseil auprès de la direction générale, notamment sur les évolutions du positionnement, les enjeux de réputation et les actions ponctuelles sensibles.

Au quotidien, ses responsabilités couvrent un large périmètre. Il définit les orientations de communication, supervise la création des supports, organise les événements, pilote les prestataires et développe des relations avec les médias et les partenaires externes. Il suit également les indicateurs de performance pour évaluer l’impact des actions menées, contrôle les budgets et produit un reporting régulier. En parallèle, il encadre les équipes de communication, accompagne leur développement et s’assure du bon fonctionnement du service.

Le métier demande une solide maîtrise des différents leviers de communication, une bonne culture digitale, une connaissance des outils de création et une aisance dans la conduite de projets. Il faut aussi savoir naviguer entre stratégie, gestion opérationnelle et représentation externe. La capacité à gérer les situations de crise, à convaincre et à fédérer est essentielle, tout comme la rigueur dans le suivi budgétaire et la cohérence des messages. La dimension relationnelle est forte, car le poste implique des échanges réguliers avec la direction, les équipes internes, les agences, les médias et des interlocuteurs institutionnels.

Les débouchés se trouvent surtout dans les grandes structures privées ou publiques : groupes internationaux, entreprises, institutions ou associations. Le poste existe aussi en agence, dans des environnements de communication, de relations publiques ou d’événementiel. Selon la taille de la structure, les missions peuvent être plus stratégiques ou davantage opérationnelles. Dans une organisation plus réduite, le poste peut prendre la forme de responsable de la communication, avec un périmètre centré sur l’exécution et la gestion quotidienne des actions.
missions_principales: Définir la stratégie de communication et le plan annuel.
Conseiller la direction générale sur l’image, le positionnement et les enjeux de marque.
Piloter la communication interne, externe, corporate, digitale et presse.
Superviser la création des supports et garantir la cohérence des messages.
Élaborer et suivre la stratégie événementielle et les relations publiques.
competences_hard_skills: Maîtrise de la communication corporate, interne, externe, RP et de crise.
Excellente culture digitale, médias sociaux et communication en ligne.
Connaissance de la chaîne graphique et de l’édition de supports print et digitaux.
Maîtrise des procédures budgétaires, du contrôle des coûts et du reporting.
Capacité à conduire des projets et à piloter des prestataires.
competences_soft_skills: Organisation, rigueur et sens des priorités.

descriptif_general:
A Financial Analyst evaluates financial data to support strategic decision-making within companies, banks or investment firms. Working at the intersection of finance, strategy and data analysis, this role involves assessing financial performance, analyzing investment opportunities and building financial models to guide business decisions.
Financial analysts play a key role in helping organizations understand market trends, optimize financial performance and identify growth opportunities. In global financial markets, this position requires strong expertise in financial modelling, valuation techniques and data analysis to provide accurate insights for senior management, investors and stakeholders.

Key responsibilities
• Analyze financial statements and corporate performance indicators
• Build financial models and forecast scenarios
• Conduct company valuation using financial modelling techniques
• Evaluate investment opportunities and financial risks
• Monitor market trends and industry developments
• Prepare financial reports and strategic recommendations for decision-makers

Most required skills
• Financial modelling and valuation technique
• Strong analytical and quantitative skills
• Financial statement analysis
• Data analysis and interpretation
• Strategic thinking and problem-solving
• Communication and presentation skills

descriptif_general:

Working in investment banks, advisory firms or corporate finance departments, this role focuses on evaluating the financial and strategic implications of potential deals.
M&A analysts conduct detailed financial analysis, build valuation models and assess the strategic fit between companies involved in a transaction. Their work helps organizations identify growth opportunities, optimize corporate structures and execute complex deals in highly competitive global markets.

Key responsibilities
• Conduct financial analysis of acquisition targets
• Perform company valuation and deal modelling
• Analyze market conditions and industry trends
• Support due diligence processes during transactions
• Prepare financial reports and transaction presentations
• Assist in structuring mergers and acquisition deals

Most required skills
• M&A financial modelling and valuation
• Corporate finance expertise
• Strategic and analytical thinking
• Financial due diligence capabilities

title: Risk manager
descriptif_court: As Risk Manager you will be responsible for identifying, assessing, and monitoring financial risks that could affect the stability and performance of a banking
descriptif_general:
As Risk Manager you will be responsible for identifying, assessing, and monitoring financial risks that could affect the stability and performance of a banking institution. Positioned at the intersection of financial analysis, regulatory compliance, and strategic decision-making, this role ensures that risks related to markets, credit exposure, liquidity, or operations are properly evaluated and managed.
In the banking ecosystem, risk management is essential to maintain financial stability and support sustainable growth. As a risk manager, you will play a key role in analyzing risk exposure, designing mitigation strategies, and supporting strategic financial decisions that protect the institution while enabling responsible business development.

Key responsibilities
• Identify and assess financial risks related to market movements, credit exposure, liquidity constraints, and operational processes.
• Evaluate the impact of market fluctuations on portfolios, investments, and financial products.
• Conduct quantitative risk analysis using financial models, stress tests, and scenario simulations.
• Produce risk reports and dashboards for senior management, highlighting potential threats and strategic recommendations.
• Collaborate with business units (trading desks, corporate finance teams, treasury, compliance) to integrate risk considerations into financial decisions.
• Contribute to strategic decision-making by advising leadership on risk appetite, capital allocation, and financial resilience.

Most required skills
• Quantitative and analytical skills, to assess financial risks, interpret complex datasets, and develop models used to evaluate market.
• Financial markets and banking expertise, to understand financial instruments, portfolio dynamics, and the impact of market fluctuations on banking activities and investment strategies.
• Risk management methodologies, to identify, measure, and monitor different types of risks including credit risk, market risk, liquidity risk, and operational risk.
• Regulatory and compliance knowledge, to ensure that risk management practices align with banking regulations and international financial standards.
• Strategic thinking and problem-solving abilities, to anticipate potential financial threats.

descriptif_general:

- Develop and design brand guidelines (visual identity, tone of voice, storytelling) and ensure consistency across all touchpoints

- Proficiency in marketing and sales policy (universe, market, products, distribution channels)
- Good knowledge of digital marketing & communication techniques
- General knowledge of purchasing behavior, analysis and interpretation of quantitative and qualitative studies
- Project management

- Team leadership

descriptif_general:
As a Supply Chain Manager, you will lead end-to-end supply chain strategy for multinational corporations, blending operational excellence, digital transformation, and sustainability. Your role will be to orchestrate logistics, procurement and distribution networks ensuring alignment with the company’s business goals.
The Supply Chain Manager plays a central role in managing end-to-end logistics operations, aligning supply chain strategies with business goals, and driving cost efficiency, resilience, and innovation across global networks. As head of cross-functional teams, you will lead flow of goods, information and finances and play a key role in building global strategies.

descriptif_general:
As a Purchasing Manager, you will define and drive the company’s procurement strategy to secure performance, competitiveness, and long-term value creation. Acting as a strategic partner to top management, you will oversee supplier selection, contract negotiation, risk management, and cost optimization while ensuring quality, compliance, and sustainability standards.
The Purchasing Manager plays a central role in aligning sourcing strategies with corporate objectives, managing supplier relationships globally, and leading procurement teams to deliver measurable impact across the organization.

Key responsibilities
• Define and implement the company’s purchasing strategy
• Identify, evaluate, and select suppliers at national and international level
• Lead contract negotiations (pricing, service levels, terms & conditions)
• Monitor procurement budgets and optimize total cost of ownership (TCO)
• Anticipate supply risks and ensure continuity of operations
• Integrate CSR and sustainable procurement policies
• Supervise and develop purchasing teams

Most required skills
• Strong negotiation and contract management expertise
• Strategic sourcing and cost analysis capabilities
• Knowledge of procurement regulations and compliance standards
• Mastery of ERP and procurement software
• Risk management and anticipation skills
• Leadership and cross-functional coordination skills
• International supplier management experience

title: Data analyst
descriptif_court: As data analyst you will play a key role in helping companies and organizations make informed business decisions based on data. Collecting, processing and inter
descriptif_general:
As data analyst you will play a key role in helping companies and organizations make informed business decisions based on data. Collecting, processing and interpreting large volumes of data will let you transform raw information into actionable and accurate insights that support business efficiency and innovation.
Working at the intersection of business and technology, the Data Analyst collaborates with multiple departments such as marketing, finance, operations or product teams. As a main mission, the data analyst identifies trends, measures performance and delivers clear data-driven recommendations to top management.

Key responsibilities
• Collect and consolidate data from multiple sources such as databases, internal systems or external platforms.
• Clean, structure and prepare datasets to ensure reliability.
• Create dashboards, reports and visualizations to communicate insights clearly to decision-makers.
• Support business and marketing teams by translating analytical findings into actionable and accurate recommendations.
• Monitor KPIs and analyze the impact of strategic initiatives.
• Collaborate with data scientists, engineers and business stakeholders to improve data usage.

Most required skills
• Strong data analysis and statistical expertise, to collect, clean and interpret large datasets and identify patterns, trends and actionable insights that support business decision-making.
• Business and analytical understanding, enabling the translation of data insights into strategic recommendations that support marketing, finance, operations or product development.
• Technical proficiency in data tools and programming, including SQL for database querying, Python or R for data analysis, and visualization tools such as Tableau or Power BI to transform complex data into clear dashboards and reports.
• Data governance and quality awareness, ensuring responsible use of data and, compliance with privacy regulations.
• Critical thinking and problem-solving abilities, allowing analysts to question data sources, identify anomalies, test hypotheses and generate reliable insights for decision-making.

descriptif_general:

Working closely with commercial, data analytics and customer experience teams, the airline marketing manager designs campaigns that reflect evolving travel behaviors and global aviation trends. In the air transport industry, this position plays a key role in enhancing airline visibility, improving passenger engagement and supporting long-term revenue growth.

descriptif_general:
As an Asset Manager you will oversee investment portfolios on behalf of clients such as financial institutions, companies, or private investors. Working at the intersection of financial analysis, portfolio management, and investment strategy, this role ensures that assets are allocated efficiently to generate sustainable returns while managing financial risks.
In the financial ecosystem, asset management plays a central role in wealth creation and capital allocation. You will analyze financial markets, identify investment opportunities, and design portfolio strategies that balance performance, diversification, and risk management.

Key responsibilities
• Manage and optimize investment portfolios, ensuring alignment with clients’ financial objectives and risk profiles.
• Analyze financial markets and economic trends to identify profitable investment opportunities.
• Design investment strategies across asset classes such as equities, bonds, or alternative investments.
• Help clients meet their long-term asset goals through investment and portfolio management
• Conduct financial and quantitative analysis to evaluate securities and investment funds.
• Ensure compliance with financial regulations and internal investment policies.

Most required skills
• Financial analysis and valuation skills, to assess investment opportunities and evaluate asset performance.
• Portfolio management expertise, to design diversified investment strategies aligned with risk-return objectives.
• Financial markets knowledge, to understand asset classes, market trends, and investment dynamics.
• Communication and client relationship skills, to explain investment strategies and build long-term trust.

• Quantitative and analytical abilities, to interpret financial data and support investment decisions.
• Strategic thinking and decision-making, to adapt portfolio strategies to changing market conditions.

descriptif_general:

• Advise organizations on AI strategies aligned with business objectives and digital transformation initiatives
• Support companies in integrating AI into existing processes and decision-making frameworks
• Monitor and evaluating the performance of AI solutions and improving models over time
• Guide organizations in AI integration and transformation
• Ensure ethical, responsible and compliant use of artificial intelligence technologies

Most required skills
• Strong expertise in artificial intelligence and machine learning, including the ability to design, evaluate and deploy AI models that solve complex business challenges.
• Technical proficiency in programming and data science tools, such as Python, machine learning frameworks and data processing platforms used to build AI-driven solutions.
• Strategic and business consulting capabilities, enabling the identification of AI opportunities, the development of data-driven strategies and the alignment of AI initiatives with organizational objectives.
• Communication and stakeholder management skills, allowing consultants to translate complex AI concepts into clear recommendations for executives, project teams and non-technical decision-makers.
• Awareness of ethical AI, governance and data regulation frameworks, ensuring responsible use of artificial intelligence and compliance with evolving regulatory standards.

title: Trafic Manager
descriptif_court: A Traffic Manager specializes in digital acquisition strategies designed to generate qualified website traffic and improve online conversion rates. This perform
descriptif_general:
A Traffic Manager specializes in digital acquisition strategies designed to generate qualified website traffic and improve online conversion rates. This performance-focused role involves managing paid advertising campaigns across platforms such as Google Ads, Meta Ads, and other programmatic advertising channels. Traffic Managers analyze campaign data in real time to optimize targeting, advertising creatives, and budget allocation. They collaborate with digital marketing teams to ensure campaigns drive measurable business outcomes. In a data-driven marketing environment, Traffic Managers play a critical role in maximizing return on advertising investment and supporting online business growth.

Key Responsibilities
• Manage digital advertising campaigns: plan, launch, and optimize paid advertising campaigns across search engines and social platforms.
• Drive website traffic acquisition: develop strategies to attract target audiences to company websites or digital platforms.
• Optimize campaign performance: continuously adjusting bids, targeting, and creatives to improve campaign results.
• Monitor key marketing metrics: track KPIs such as click-through rates, conversions, and cost-per-acquisition, ROI.
• Collaborate with marketing teams: work with content and digital teams to ensure campaign consistency and effectiveness.
• Manage advertising budgets: allocate and monitor campaign budgets to maximize return on marketing investment.

Most required skills
• Performance marketing expertise: knowledge of digital acquisition channels and paid advertising platforms.
• Data analysis capabilities: ability to interpret campaign data and optimize marketing strategies.
• Advertising platform management: experience using tools such as Google Ads, Meta Ads, and analytics platforms.
• Data-driven vision: precision in monitoring campaign metrics and adjusting strategies, based on results.
• Conversion optimization: ability to improve user journeys and maximize digital conversion rates.
• Problem-solving mindset: capacity to quickly identify performance issues and implement corrective actions.

title: Profit Center Manager
descriptif_court: As a profit center manager, you will lead business units with full responsibility for their financial performance and strategic development. Acting as an entrep
descriptif_general:
As a profit center manager, you will lead business units with full responsibility for their financial performance and strategic development. Acting as an entrepreneur within the organization, you manage revenue, costs, and profitability through clear P&L ownership. As a manager, you coordinate cross-functional teams and ensure alignment between commercial, operational, and strategic objectives. This role requires a strong balance between business development and operational excellence.

Key responsibilities
• Develop and implement business strategies: define the strategic roadmap of the profit center aligned with overall company objectives
• Manage financial performance: oversee revenue, costs, and profitability through P&L management and performance monitoring
• Lead and coordinate teams: manage cross-functional teams to ensure alignment, efficiency, and achievement of business goals
• Drive business development: identify new market opportunities, expand client portfolios, and increase revenue streams
• Monitor operational performance: track KPIs and optimize processes to improve efficiency and service quality
• Ensure reporting and decision-making: analyze performance data and provide insights to support strategic decisions

Most required skills

• Business and financial acumen: strong ability to manage P&L, analyze profitability, and optimize costs and revenues
• Strategic and operational management: capacity to define vision while ensuring efficient execution
• Leadership and team management: ability to lead multidisciplinary teams and drive performance
• Commercial mindset: strong focus on growth, client acquisition, and market development
• Analytical and decision-making skills: using data to guide strategy and improve results
• Adaptability and problem-solving: ability to operate in dynamic and competitive environments

title: Venture Capital Analyst
descriptif_court: The Venture Capital Analyst plays a central role in identifying and evaluating high-potential startups for investment. They analyze business models, financial p
descriptif_general:
The Venture Capital Analyst plays a central role in identifying and evaluating high-potential startups for investment. They analyze business models, financial performance, and market opportunities to support investment decisions. Working closely with investors and entrepreneurs, they contribute to sourcing deals and conducting due diligence. This role requires a strong understanding of innovative ecosystems and emerging industries. It is a key entry position into venture capital, combining finance, strategy, and entrepreneurship.

Key responsibilities
• Identify investment opportunities: source and screen startups with strong growth potential across industries
• Conduct financial and strategic analysis: evaluating business models, financial projections, and market positioning
• Perform due diligence: assess risks, validate assumptions, and analyze competitive environments
• Support investment decision-making: prepare investment memos and present insights to investment committees
• Monitor portfolio performance: track KPIs and support the development of invested startups
• Conduct market research: analyze industry trends, emerging technologies, and innovation ecosystems

Most required skills
• Financial analysis and valuation: ability to assess startups and understand investment metrics
• Market and trend analysis: strong understanding of innovation ecosystems and emerging sectors
• Strategic thinking: capacity to evaluate business models and long-term potential
• Analytical and research skills: ability to synthesize complex information into actionable insights
• Communication and storytelling: presenting investment opportunities clearly and convincingly
• Curiosity and entrepreneurial mindset: strong interest in startups and innovation-driven environments

title: Country Manager
descriptif_court: As a Country Manager, you are responsible for developing and executing a company’s strategy within a specific market. You oversee business operations, adapt glo
descriptif_general:
As a Country Manager, you are responsible for developing and executing a company’s strategy within a specific market. You oversee business operations, adapt global strategies to local environments, and ensure commercial performance. This role requires strong analytical skills, cultural understanding, and leadership capabilities. You coordinate local teams, manage partnerships, and identify growth opportunities. By aligning headquarters’ objectives with local market realities, Country Managers play a key role in driving international expansion and long-term business success.

Key Responsibilities
• Develop country-level business strategies: define market-specific strategies aligned with global objectives, local market dynamics, and long-term growth targets.
• Drive market entry and expansion initiatives: identify opportunities, assess risks, and implement market entry strategies to establish and grow the company’s presence.
• Manage local operations and performance: oversee day-to-day business activities, ensuring operational efficiency and achievement of financial and commercial objectives.
• Coordinate cross-functional teams: collaborate with sales, marketing, supply chain, and finance teams to ensure alignment between global strategy and local execution.
• Build and manage strategic partnerships: develop relationships with key stakeholders, distributors, and partners to strengthen market positioning and business development.

Most required skills
• International business strategy and market analysis: ability to assess global markets, identify opportunities, and design strategies adapted to local economic and competitive environments.
• Adaptability in complex global environments: capacity to navigate uncertainty, adjust strategies quickly, and operate effectively in fast-changing international markets.
• Cross-cultural management and communication: capability to collaborate effectively across cultures and lead teams in diverse international contexts.
• Leadership and team management: strong ability to lead, motivate, and coordinate cross-functional teams to achieve business objectives.
• Financial and operational acumen: understanding of financial performance, budgeting, and operational processes to ensure business efficiency and profitability

title: Business Development Manager
descriptif_court: As a Business Development Manager your role will be to identify growth opportunities and drive international expansion by developing new markets, partnerships,
descriptif_general:
As a Business Development Manager your role will be to identify growth opportunities and drive international expansion by developing new markets, partnerships, and client relationships. This role combines strategic analysis with commercial execution, requiring a strong understanding of market dynamics and customer needs. Business Development Managers analyze potential markets, design entry strategies, and negotiate deals with partners. In an international context, they play a key role in expanding a company’s global footprint and ensuring sustainable business growth.

Key Responsibilities
• Develop business development strategies: define growth strategies aligned with company objectives, targeting new markets, clients, and revenue opportunities.
• Identify and assess market opportunities: analyze market trends, customer needs, and competitive landscapes to prioritize high-potential business segments.
• Build and manage client relationships: establish and maintain strong partnerships with clients, distributors, and strategic stakeholders to support long-term growth.
• Coordinate cross-functional initiatives: collaborate with sales, marketing, and product teams to ensure alignment between market needs and business offerings.
• Monitor market trends and competitive dynamics: stay informed about industry developments, emerging opportunities, and competitor strategies to adapt positioning.

Most required skills
• Business development strategy and market analysis: ability to identify growth opportunities and design strategies based on market insights and business objectives.
• Negotiation and relationship management: strong capability to build trust, manage partnerships, and successfully negotiate commercial agreements.
• Commercial and financial acumen: understanding of revenue models, pricing strategies, and financial performance to drive sustainable growth.
• Project and stakeholder management: strong organizational skills to coordinate multiple initiatives and align internal and external stakeholders.
• Adaptability in dynamic business environments: capacity to adjust strategies quickly and operate effectively in fast-changing and competitive markets.

title: Stadium Manager
descriptif_court: As stadium manager you will be responsible for the strategic, operational, and commercial management of a sports venue. Acting as the central coordinator of the
descriptif_general:
As stadium manager you will be responsible for the strategic, operational, and commercial management of a sports venue. Acting as the central coordinator of the stadium ecosystem, you oversee all activities related to infrastructure operations, event delivery, revenue optimization, safety, and stakeholder coordination.
Considering that nowadays stadiums are no longer just sport facilities, but multifunctional business hubs hosting matches, concerts, corporate events and large-scale entertainment moments, the stadium manager ensures that the venue operates efficiently, generates sustainable revenue and delivers high quality fan experience.

Key responsibilities
• Oversee the daily operations of the stadium, ensuring technical, logistical, and facility management excellence across all events and non-event days.
• Coordinate sporting events, concerts, and corporate functions, ensuring seamless execution, compliance with safety regulations, and premium audience experience.
• Develop and implement strategies to maximize revenue streams, including ticketing, hospitality, sponsorship activation, merchandising, and venue rentals.
• Manage operational budgets, monitor financial performance, negotiate contracts with suppliers and service providers, and ensure cost control.
• Lead multidisciplinary teams (operations, security, marketing, hospitality, technical staff) and collaborate with clubs, federations, sponsors, and local authorities.

Most required skills
• Operational and logistical expertise, with strong organizational skills to manage large-scale and complex events.
• Commercial and financial acumen, understanding stadium business models, revenue streams, sponsorship structures and cost management.
• Fan experience awareness and marketing strategies to engage audiences and manage hospitality services.
• Leadership and communication skills with professional English proficiency for collaborations in global sport environments.
• Flexibility and crisis management to react quickly to operational challenges and manage unforeseen situations effectively.
• Legal knowledge of compliance frameworks and contractual safety obligations.

title: Sponsorship Manager
descriptif_court: The Sponsorship Manager is responsible for developing, negotiating, and activating partnership agreements between sport organizations and corporate brands. Posi
descriptif_general:
The Sponsorship Manager is responsible for developing, negotiating, and activating partnership agreements between sport organizations and corporate brands. Positioned at the intersection of marketing, business development, and brand strategy, this role ensures that sponsorship agreements generate measurable value for both the rights holder (club, federation, event organizer) and the sponsoring partner.
In a sport business ecosystem, sponsorships are core of revenue growth. As a sponsorship manager, you will play a key role in identifying commercial opportunities, structuring partnership packages, and delivering impactful activations that strengthen brand visibility and performance.

Key responsibilities
• Design and implement sponsorship strategies aligned with the organization’s commercial objectives and brand positioning.
• Develop tailored sponsorship proposals and identify new potential sponsors, negotiating contracts and securing long-term agreements.
• Act as the main contact point for sponsors and ensure satisfaction and upselling opportunities.
• Ensure the good execution of sponsorship campaigns and track performance using KPIs such as media exposure, brand visibility, fan engagement and ROI.
• Collaborate with marketing and communication teams
• Ensure perfect integrations of sponsorship assets in the corporate ecosystem.

Most required skills
• Negotiation and commercial skills, to structure partnership deals, negotiate contracts and identify growth opportunities.
• Brand positioning and marketing expertise, to understand audience targeting, digital activations and integrated marketing campaigns.
• Relational intelligence and communication, to build and manage long-term and trust-based partnerships.
• Project management, to coordinate multiple activations simultaneously while meeting deadlines and budget constraints.
• Data-driven mindset, to measure sponsorship ROI and analyze data and activations performance.
• Knowledge of the sport industry ecosystem, to understand rights holders, communities and global sport business dynamics.
